##  Data Preparation

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#Reading in csv file and assigning to data frame object named "text_wide" 
text_wide <- read.csv("TextMessages.csv")
class(text_wide$Group)
text_wide$Group <-factor(text_wide$Group,levels=c(1,2))

#In case we need long format data-
text_long <- pivot_longer(
  text_wide, 
  cols= c("Baseline","Six_months"),
  names_to = "Timepoint",
  values_to = "Text_count"
  )
class(text_long$Timepoint)
text_long$Timepoint<-factor(text_long$Timepoint)

#Moving participant number to the front
text_wide <- text_wide |> relocate("Participant")
text_long <- text_long |> relocate("Participant")

```

## Visualization 1: Faceted Boxplot of text messages by Group and Time

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#Creating faceted boxplots of text messages for each group and across the
#time-points using ggplot() and geom(boxplot). We color-code by time-points and
#use facet_wrap(~Group) to display the plots side by side.

visualization1<- ggplot(
  data=text_long,
  aes(y=Text_count, 
      x=Timepoint, 
      fill=Timepoint))+
  geom_boxplot(show.legend=FALSE)+
  facet_wrap(~Group)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(from=0, to=100, by=10))+
  labs(title = "Facet Boxplots of Text Messages by Time-point and Group\n",
       y="Text Count\n",
       x="Time-point")+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

print(visualization1)

#We can compare the distributions of text messages across time-points (Baseline,
#6-months) for both groups (1,2) side by side. At baseline, both groups show
#similar distributions of text message counts, with approximately the same
#median values of 64/65. The interquartile ranges and overall spread also looks
#comparable, which suggests that the two groups had similar baseline
#characteristics.

#At 6 months, we can see a decrease in median text message counts for both
#groups, though the reduction looks to be more for group 1 (from approximately
#64 to 58) when compared to group 2 (approximately 65 to 62). There are also
#noticeable differences in variability between the groups at six months. Group 1
#has a wider distribution, with several low outliers with values below 20
#messages as well as higher counts above 75. This suggests greater variability
#in text counts among participants in Group 1. In contrast, Group 2 has a
#narrower distribution with relatively higher messaging counts, suggesting more
#consistent messaging patterns across the participants.
```

## Interpretation and conclusions

Any concluding comments in addition to individual interpretations above

### Visualization 1 conclusions

Overall, the boxplots suggest a reduction in text messaging frequency in both groups over the six-month period, with a more noticeable shift in Group 1. Additionally, Group 1 demonstrates greater variability in messaging behavior at the six-month time-point, whereas Group 2 shows a more consistent distribution. The presence of several low outliers in Group 1 suggests that changes in messaging frequency may vary considerably among individual participants.
